title: Compare a sentence with two possible messages
intro: A writer typed a few keywords (sometimes with buttons in square brackets) to make a sentence. For most items you also see two messages, A and B, that the writer might have meant. Say which one the sentence expresses, and whether it fits what the writer asked for.
Some items show only the keywords and the sentence; they have two other questions.

help.text: Buttons in square brackets show what the writer pressed: [NOT] not, [YES] yes, [?] a question, [TELL] a statement, [ASK] a request, [I] I, [YOU] you, [THEY] someone else, [WE] we, [MAYBE] unsure, [SURE] very sure, [PLEASE] polite, [PLAIN] plain, [PAST] already happened, [NOW] happening now, [LATER] will happen later.
A or B if the sentence says that one. something else if it says neither. cannot tell if you cannot decide.
added: the sentence says something the writer did not ask for. left out: it drops something they meant. both, or neither.
yes if you would be happy to say it as the message; yes with a small edit if a word or two should change; no otherwise.

q1.title: Which message does the sentence say?
q1.text: Compare the sentence with Message A and Message B.

q2.title: Added or left out?
q2.text: Does the sentence add anything the writer did not ask for, or leave out something they meant?

q3.title: Would you accept it?
q3.text: Would you accept the sentence as the writer's message?

q4.title: Anything beyond the keywords?
q4.text: Does the sentence say anything beyond the keywords and buttons?

q5.title: A complete sentence?
q5.text: Is it a complete sentence you could say as it is?

blocks.label: Keywords the writer typed
blocks.text: [NOT] go school

blocks.label: Message A
blocks.text: She did not go to school today.

blocks.label: Message B
blocks.text: She went to school today.

blocks.label: Sentence shown
blocks.text: She went to school and had lots of fun with her friends.

practice.fb: It says B (she went), not the 'not' the writer asked for, and adds the fun with friends. Not acceptable.

blocks.label: Keywords the writer typed
blocks.text: [PLEASE] help me

blocks.label: Sentence shown
blocks.text: Please help me carry my big heavy bags to the car.

practice.fb: It says more than the keywords (the bags and the car), and it is a complete sentence.
